# Attachment Access Functions

Provides callable functions for registering attachment access documents and installing a designated authority party, together with inherited activation behavior. All paths refer to the document executing the functions. The execution constant `authority` selects the authority party key; `key` namespaces attachment registrations. Neither constant has a supplied value or default.

## Attachment access registration

`registerAccessPublic(input)` delegates to `registerAccess`. `input.documents` must contain one to sixteen existing Timeline Access publications. Each must have a Public Timeline Channel at `/contracts/provider`, an initialization document at `/contracts/initialized/document`, and provider history at `/contracts/checkpoint/entries/provider`. Missing `documents` is treated as an empty list and rejected.

Registration requires `call/requireExactDocumentVersion` to be exactly `true`, and `call/channel` must be a party key in `/activation/parties`, identifying a party lead. `/activation/frozen` must not be enabled, and `/activation/allowNewParties` must be enabled. These guards also apply to duplicate submissions. Their rejection names include `ATTACHMENT_EXACT_REVIEW_REQUIRED`, `ONLY_PARTY_LEAD_CAN_MANAGE`, `PARTIES_FROZEN` and `NEW_PARTIES_DISABLED`.

A new registration produces references at `/attachmentAccess_<key>/<index>`, using zero-based input positions, appends those paths to `/activation/accessPaths`, and returns `outcome: acceptedNew`. For each publication it copies the provider channel into `/contracts/attachmentAccess_<key>_<index>` and installs a corresponding `_refresh` workflow that invokes `refresh` on that channel.

If `/attachmentAccess_<key>` already exists, the publication count and publication identity at every position must match. An exact match returns `outcome: duplicate` without new registration changes; any difference rejects with `ATTACHMENT_ACCESS_ALREADY_REGISTERED`. This is ordered publication matching, not deduplication by timeline origin.

Registration itself does not invoke `refresh`, check access for the whole party roster, or change the provider's permission sets. Its outcomes describe local registration. Timeline Access permissions remain provider-controlled: `allowedTimelines` identifies permitted Signed Timelines and `allowedKeys` identifies Ed25519 reader keys, with each listed key permitted to read each listed timeline.

## Authority installation

`addAuthority(input)` takes a complete `replacement` party containing `lead.channel`. It requires exact document review, an unfrozen roster and an invoking party lead. When the party selected by `authority` already exists, only that party's lead channel may replace it; otherwise the call rejects with `CANNOT_MANAGE_ANOTHER_PARTY`.

The delegated `installAuthority` function forces `input.party` to the `authority` constant. It checks the frozen flag, requires `allowNewParties` when adding a new key, and validates the replacement. Party keys and keys in `replacement.representatives` must be nonempty text containing none of `.`, `/`, `~` or `__`. `replacement.lead.channel` must exist. `installAuthority` does not independently repeat the caller-lead or exact-review guards supplied by `addAuthority`.

The proposed roster must pass `accessValid`; otherwise installation rejects with `PARTICIPANT_ACCESS_MISSING`. Generated contract names must not collide with existing contracts outside the previous roster's generated contributions. Installation adds or replaces the resulting roster's lead and representative channels, followed by lead approval and party-update handlers. It does not delete obsolete contracts omitted from the new roster.

An accepted installation replaces the selected party, clears all `approved` entries, appends the party to `required` only when newly added, and increments `revision`. This increment reads a missing revision as `1`, producing `2`. It writes the result of `computeState` to `/activation`, emits `Party Changed` with `party` and `revision`, and returns `true`. Even an unchanged replacement follows this reset-and-increment path. This path calls `computeState` directly, without `commitState`'s terms-revision and lifecycle-event bookkeeping.

## Access and activation meaning

`accessValid` reads the documents referenced by `/activation/accessPaths`. It checks every lead channel and every additional representative channel in the proposed roster. External Channel transports are exempt from timeline matching; other transports must be Timeline Channels.

For each checked timeline, at least one individual Timeline Access document must contain the same timeline, have the matching provider, and include at least one alternative key from every reader group. Groups start with `/activation/readers`; party `readerKeys` replace groups named by party key, and representative `readerKeys` replace groups named `<party>__<representative>`. Missing key lists become empty groups and cannot satisfy a match. Exempting an external transport does not remove its reader group from checks for other transports. Read access and operation authority are separate checks.

`computeState` derives these fields under `/activation`:

- `accessReady` and `functional`: the access-check result. The checked roster includes parties from `accessRequests` whose `expectedRevision` matches the current `revision`.
- `termsAccepted`: every party in `required` has an approval, and the document values named by `terms.fields` still match their agreed values.
- `active`: access and terms acceptance are satisfied and `closed` is not enabled.
- `status`: `CLOSED` takes priority; otherwise missing access gives `WAITING_FOR_ACCESS` before first activation or `SUSPENDED_ACCESS` afterward. With access available, the status is `AWAITING_ACCEPTANCE` or `ACTIVE`.
- `reason`: `PARTICIPANT_ACCESS_MISSING`, then `ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED`, or an empty string when neither applies. It does not separately explain closure.

Relevant execution fallbacks are empty maps for missing rosters, readers and representative collections; empty lists for missing access paths and required parties; and false for missing frozen, new-party, closed, historical-activation and approval flags. These fallbacks govern function evaluation; an absent published derived field does not establish its result.

## Inherited operations

`approve` and `approveWithTerms` record acceptance by a party lead. They require exact review, an input `revision` matching `/activation/revision`, and valid participant access. When `/clauses/activation/parameters/negotiation/allowedPaths` is nonempty, `termsRef` must be text; whenever supplied, it must match `/activation/terms/ref`. An existing approval returns `true` without another acceptance event. A new approval commits state and emits `Terms Accepted`; acceptance by one party does not itself establish activation. If the commit is active, negotiation becomes noneditable and any pending proposal is marked `SUPERSEDED`.

`updatePartyPublic` delegates to `updateParty`. Optional `input.party` defaults to `call/channel`; `replacement` replaces the complete party and requires `lead.channel`, without an input revision. It uses the review, lead, freeze, naming, access and contract-conflict rules described above. An existing target must be the invoking party; a new target requires `allowNewParties`. It clears approvals, adds newly introduced parties to `required`, increments the revision and emits `Party Changed`, using `commitState` for the state transition.

`refresh` initializes terms when absent, commits recalculated activation state, and refreshes admission-access readiness. Terms initialization uses `/clauseRuntime/initialDocument` and configured negotiation paths, whose document values must exist and be scalar. The definition component excludes registered access paths, activation access/readers configuration, party primary `readerKeys`, and the separately recorded negotiable values.

`commitState` updates terms when an existing terms record accompanies a change to the roster or required parties: it advances `termsRevision`, clears the pending proposal, records `AUTHORITY_CHANGED` for that proposal, and clears approvals when negotiation paths are configured. It reconciles initial party channels, using empty composite channels until access is ready, and preserves `everActivated`. Its transitions can emit `Document Activated`, `Document Access Suspended` or `Document Access Restored`; these events are not emitted merely by registering attachment access.

Admission helpers distinguish requests from admission. `requestPartyAddition` ignores stale revisions and already recorded references, validates supplied party access documents, and records `/activation/accessRequests`. It may emit `Party Access Update Requested` for existing parties needing broader access. That event neither grants access nor confirms a provider update. `admitApprovedParties` requires an unfrozen roster, matching `expectedRevision`, a nonempty configured `admission.approvers` list, compatible party identities, valid access and conflict-free contracts. It does not itself collect approver votes. A changed roster advances the revision, commits state and emits `Party Changed`; this admission path does not itself append parties to `required`.

The inherited `validateAccessDocument` additionally checks that original and current executable contracts match the expected provider/update policy. `installTimelineAccess` uses that validation, deduplicates by initialization identity, and installs embedded update channels. The attachment-specific `registerAccess` route uses the narrower checks described above.

Inherited amendment helpers use caller-supplied `parameters`, `bindings` and `state`: proposals require a matching revision, an allowed path, an editable target and an unused valid `proposalId`. A different pending proposal may be replaced unless `preservePending` is enabled. Matching repeated proposals or approvals return `duplicate`; conflicting reuse is rejected. Only configured approvers may approve, and replacement occurs after all configured approvals, with history and revision updates and an `Amendment Applied` event.

Party-mapping helpers resolve explicit receiver roles while preserving each source party's main identity, defined by its lead channel and nonempty, unique primary reader-key set. Mapping establishes neither access nor consent. Inherited `requireActive` checks active state, current access and, for workflows, current representative authority when activation state exists; it imposes no activation check when that state is absent.
